cards.text: Moses, Israel's leader, is preaching his heart out to all Israel. He's already laid out the blessings and the curses, the whole deal. Now he looks way down the road, to a day when it's all come true and Israel is banished among the nations, calling every word of this to mind.

cards.question: Israel is scattered among the nations, remembering everything Moses said. What does Moses say they and their children do next?

answers.text: Return to the LORD and obey His voice
Build a new altar in that far land
Send messengers back to find Moses

cards.text: And not halfway, either. With all their heart and all their soul, Moses says. Then it's God's move.

cards.question: The people have returned to the LORD, but they're still scattered across all the nations. What does Moses say the LORD will do?

answers.text: Gather them from all the nations
Send them a new king out there

cards.text: Even if they're banished to the farthest horizon, He will gather them and bring them back from there. Friend, I lived in the BACK of a junk drawer for years, and the Most High still found me.
Then the LORD brings them into the land their fathers possessed, and they take possession of it again.

cards.question: True or false: Moses says that back in the land, they'll end up with less than their fathers had.

cards.text: Then Moses says the LORD will circumcise their hearts, and the hearts of their descendants. And notice who's doing it, friend. Not them. The LORD.

cards.question: Once the LORD circumcises their hearts, what does Moses say the people will do?

answers.text: Love Him with all their heart and soul
Forget every curse they ever heard
Never wander from the land again

cards.text: And all those curses Moses laid out? They don't just vanish. They get a NEW ADDRESS.

cards.question: Where does Moses say the LORD will put all these curses?

answers.text: On the enemies who hate and persecute them
On the leaders who led them astray
On the lands where they were scattered

cards.text: Israel will again obey the voice of the LORD, and He makes them abound in everything: their work, their children, their livestock, their crops. Friend, that's more overflow than my oven on its BEST day, and my oven has had some days.

cards.question: Moses says the LORD will again ___ in their prosperity, just as He did with their fathers.
True or false: Moses says all these blessings come no matter how Israel lives.

cards.text: Now Moses talks about the commandment he's giving them today. So is this some impossible thing they'll never manage?

cards.question: True or false: Moses says the commandment he gives them today is too difficult for them.

cards.text: Moses says it's not up in heaven, so nobody has to ask who's going to climb up there and get it for them.

cards.question: True or false: Moses says someone will have to cross the sea to get the commandment for them.
The commandment isn't up in heaven or across the sea. So where does Moses say the word is?

answers.text: In their mouth and in their heart
With the priests in the tabernacle
Stored up for the next generation

cards.text: Very near, Moses says. Friend, that's closer than my mustache, and my mustache is attached to my FACE.
Then Moses lays it all out: "See, I have set before you today life and prosperity, as well as death and disaster."

cards.question: On the life side, what is Moses commanding them to do today?

answers.text: Love the LORD and walk in His ways
Gather gold and build strong cities
Offer a sacrifice every single morning

cards.question: True or false: Moses says keeping the LORD's commandments is so they may live and increase in the land.

cards.text: But then there's the other road. Their heart turns away, they don't listen, and they get drawn away to bow down to other gods.

cards.question: If Israel turns away to other gods, what does Moses declare will happen to them?

answers.text: They will wander forty more years

cards.text: No long days in the land they're crossing the Jordan to possess. Same dough, same oven, friend. One road comes out golden, and the other comes out BURNT.
Moses is ready to wrap this sermon up. And he wants witnesses for what he's set before them today.

cards.question: Who does Moses call as witnesses against Israel today?
Moses has set life and death before them. He tells them to choose ___ so that they and their descendants may live.

cards.text: He doesn't just list the options and walk away. That's my oven timer going off and YELLING which tray to pull.

cards.question: Moses says choosing life means loving the LORD and obeying Him and holding fast to Him. Then he tells them why. What does he say the LORD is to them?

cards.text: And He will prolong their life in the land He swore to give their fathers: Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, the fathers of Israel. Choose life, hold fast to Him, because He is your life. That's how Moses lands it.

findings.problem: The punchline "and my oven has had some days" is ambiguous. The phrase usually means rough days, but it follows "on its BEST day," so the baker has to stop and work out whether the oven's days were good or bad. The joke doesn't land cleanly.

rule.text: It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "hesitate" doesn't work in the sentence. "The LORD will again hesitate in their prosperity" isn't a believable reading, so it stands out as filler and the right answer is easy to spot by elimination. A wrong answer should be another real way God could respond to their prosperity.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The joke mixes two images. "Same dough, same oven" is the cookie comparison, but "One road comes out golden" carries over the road picture from card 10. Roads don't come out of ovens. The joke should use the oven image alone.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: The question says "choosing life means loving the LORD and obeying Him and holding fast to Him." In Deut 30:19-20, loving, obeying and holding fast come after "so that": they are what choosing life leads to, not what it means. The card changes how the two ideas connect.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences, plus the closing "That's how Moses lands it." Story cards after the opening card are limited to two sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The line "Choose life, hold fast to Him, because He is your life. That's how Moses lands it." goes back over cards 15 and 17 and adds nothing new. Only the first sentence, about the land sworn to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, moves the passage forward.
